records.change: "digged down a wall" becomes "houghed oxen"

records.change: "gathering of the people" becomes "obedience of peoples"

records.change: "the LORD hath sworn" becomes "hand is on the throne of Jah"

records.change: "keep his virgin" becomes "keep his own virginity"
records.note: Translation choice, as in verse 36: Darby reads parthenos as the man's own virginity rather than a woman in his charge.

records.change: "Jesus Christ our Lord" becomes "Jesus our Lord"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: "the gospel of Christ" becomes "the glad tidings"
records.note: "Of Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: Omits "for the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof"
records.note: The repeated quotation is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; it stands in verse 26.

records.change: Omits "Take, eat" and "broken"
records.note: Both are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; the body is still given "for you".

records.change: Omits "unworthily" and "Lord's" before "body"
records.note: Both are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; verse 27 still has "unworthily" and "the body and blood of the Lord".

records.change: "the second man is the Lord from heaven" loses "the Lord"
records.note: "The Lord" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or the first hand of Ephesius; the second man is still "out of heaven".

records.change: "Jesus Christ" bracketed in "the Lord Jesus Christ"
records.note: "Jesus Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. Darby keeps the words in brackets as doubtful.

records.change: Omits the subscription about Philippi and Stephanas
records.note: The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: Clauses reordered; second "and salvation" dropped
records.note: Darby follows the order of P46, Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus, which differs from the Textus Receptus and lacks the second "and salvation". The thought of comfort for their salvation is kept.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: "Lord" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Our" and "Christ" are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the subscription
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: Omits "in Christ" after "confirmed before of God"
records.note: "In Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: "an heir of God through Christ" becomes "heir also through God"
records.note: The Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus have "of God through Christ"; P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus have "through God". Christ's part in sonship stands in verses 4-6.

records.change: "in Christ Jesus" bracketed as doubtful
records.note: The words are in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46 or Vaticanus. Darby keeps the words in brackets as doubtful.

records.change: Omits the subscription "To the Galatians written from Rome"
records.note: The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: Omits "by Jesus Christ" as creator
records.note: "By Jesus Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. Creation through Christ is stated in Colossians 1:16 and John 1:3.

records.change: "of our Lord Jesus Christ" bracketed as doubtful
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. Darby keeps the words in brackets as doubtful.

records.change: "the fruit of the Spirit" becomes "the fruit of the light"
records.note: The Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus have "Spirit", likely from Galatians 5:22; P49, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus have "light", matching verse 8.

records.change: "the fear of God" becomes "[the] fear of Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "God"; P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus and most manuscripts have "Christ".

records.change: "the Lord" becomes "the Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "the Lord"; P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority have "Christ".

records.change: "of his flesh, and of his bones" bracketed as doubtful
records.note: The words, echoing Genesis 2:23, are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Darby keeps the words in brackets as doubtful.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the subscription
records.note: The closing "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: Verses 16 and 17 are in the reverse order
records.note: Darby follows Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus, which put the preachers "of love" first; the Textus Receptus puts those "of contention" first. Nothing is lost.

records.change: "the work of Christ" becomes "the work"
records.note: "Of Christ" is in most manuscripts and the Textus Receptus; Darby follows Ephraemi (C), which has "the work" alone. The work is plainly Christ's.

records.change: Omits "rule" and "let us mind the same thing"
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P16, P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; the call to be of one mind stands in 2:2.

records.change: "through Christ" becomes "in him"
records.note: The Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus name Christ; Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus have only "him". The referent is plainly Christ.

records.change: "with you all. Amen" becomes "with your spirit. Amen"; subscription omitted
records.note: "With your spirit" is the reading of P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus. The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: "and the Lord Jesus Christ" bracketed in the greeting
records.note: The words are in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Ephraemi and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus, Bezae and some others. Darby keeps the words in brackets as doubtful.

records.change: Omits "through his blood"
records.note: The phrase is in some later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or the Byzantine majority; it is likely from Ephesians 1:7. Redemption by his blood is stated in Colossians 1:20.

records.change: "it pleased the Father" becomes "the fulness [of the Godhead] was pleased"
records.note: The Greek has neither "the Father" nor "of the Godhead"; the KJV supplies the one (in italics), Darby the other (in brackets, from 2:9). Darby makes the fulness the subject.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Christ"
records.note: "Jesus" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: Omits "and of the Father, and of Christ"
records.note: Darby reads "the mystery of God" alone, with a few late witnesses. The Textus Receptus has "of God, and of the Father, and of Christ"; P46 and Vaticanus have "of God, Christ", calling Christ the mystery of God. 1:27 still says the mystery is Christ in you.

records.change: "the peace of God" becomes "the peace of Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "God"; Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority have "Christ".

records.change: "to the Lord" becomes "to God"
records.note: The Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus have "the Lord"; P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus have "God".

records.change: "fearing God" becomes "fearing the Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "God"; P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus have "the Lord". The next verses speak of serving the Lord Christ.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the subscription
records.note: The closing "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: Omits "from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ"
records.note: The words are in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus, which Darby follows here. God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ are named earlier in the verse.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus and some later manuscripts but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the subscription
records.note: The closing "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus or the first hand of Sinaiticus. The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: "the day of Christ" becomes "the day of the Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "Christ"; Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority have "the Lord". The coming of Christ is the subject of verse 1.

records.change: Omits "as God" before "sitteth in the temple"
records.note: "As God" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; he still shows himself "that he is God".

records.change: "the Lord" becomes "the Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Jesus" is in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and other early witnesses but not in the Byzantine text or the Textus Receptus. Darby adds it.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the subscription
records.note: The closing "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the first hand of Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "Lord Jesus Christ"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and most manuscripts have "Christ Jesus".

records.change: "the only wise God" becomes "only God"
records.note: "Wise" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or the first hand of Claromontanus; it may come from Romans 16:27.

records.change: Omits "in Christ" from "I speak the truth"
records.note: "In Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Alexandrinus; it is likely from Romans 9:1.

records.change: "the Saviour of all men" becomes "preserver of all men"
records.note: Translation choice: the Greek is sōtēr (saviour) in both. Darby renders it "preserver" here, reading God's care for all men, while "specially of those that believe" keeps salvation for believers.

records.change: Omits "in spirit"
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Ephraemi.

records.change: "having damnation" becomes "being guilty"
records.note: The Greek (krima or krisis, judgment) is the same in both; "judgment" is the literal sense, the KJV's "damnation" an interpretation of it. The outcome is still condemnation.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "Lord Jesus Christ"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and most manuscripts have "Christ Jesus".

records.change: Omits "from such withdraw thyself"
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or the first hand of Claromontanus.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the subscription
records.note: The closing "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the first hand of Sinaiticus or Alexandrinus. The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: "the name of Christ" becomes "the name of [the] Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "Christ"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority have "the Lord", as in the quotation before it.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: "The Lord" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Alexandrinus; he is still the judge of the living and the dead.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the subscription
records.note: The closing "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Ephraemi. The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: Omits "mercy"; "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "grace, mercy, and peace" and "Lord Jesus Christ"; Sinaiticus and Ephraemi have "grace and peace" and "Christ Jesus".

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the subscription
records.note: The closing "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the first hand of Sinaiticus or Ephraemi. The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: Second "in the Lord" becomes "in Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "the Lord"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority have "Christ".

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the subscription
records.note: The closing "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P87 or the first hand of Sinaiticus. The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: "by himself" bracketed; omits "our"
records.note: "By himself" and "our" are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; Darby keeps "by himself" in brackets. The purging is still his own work.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P13, P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: "after the order of Melchisedec" bracketed
records.note: The words are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; Psalm 110:4 is quoted in full in 5:6 and 7:17. Darby keeps the words in brackets as doubtful.

records.change: Omits "O God"
records.note: "O God" is in some later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; it stands in verse 7.

records.change: "for ever" goes with "sat down", not with "one sacrifice"
records.note: Punctuation choice: the Greek eis to diēnekes can go with either. The KJV says the sacrifice is for ever; Darby that he sat down in perpetuity. 10:14 still says he has perfected them for ever.

records.change: Omits "in heaven"; "me in my bonds" becomes "prisoners"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "my bonds" and "in heaven"; P13, P46, Alexandrinus and others have "the prisoners" and lack "in heaven". The better and abiding possession is still promised.

records.change: Omits the subscription "Written to the Hebrews from Italy"
records.note: The subscriptions are not part of the letters; they were added by later scribes and printed in the Textus Receptus. Darby, like modern editions, leaves them out.

records.change: "the Lord hath promised" becomes "He has promised"
records.note: "The Lord" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P23, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; the subject is God, as verse 13 shows.

records.change: "God, even the Father" becomes "the Lord and Father"
records.note: The Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus have "God"; Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus have "the Lord".

records.change: Omits "through the Spirit"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P72, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; the Spirit's sanctifying work is named in 1:2.

records.change: Omits "for ever" of the word of God
records.note: "For ever" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P72, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; verse 25 still says the word abides for ever.

records.change: Adds "to salvation"
records.note: "Unto salvation" is in P72, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus but not in the Byzantine text or the Textus Receptus.

records.change: "the Lord God" becomes "[the] Lord the Christ"
records.note: The Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read "the Lord God"; P72, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus read "the Lord the Christ". The verse then applies Isaiah 8:13, said of the LORD of hosts, to Christ.

records.change: "on their part he is evil spoken of..." bracketed
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P72, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. Darby keeps the words in brackets as doubtful.

records.change: Omits "Jesus" and "Amen"
records.note: Both are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: "cast them down to hell" becomes "to the deepest pit of gloom"
records.note: Translation choice: the Greek is the verb tartaroō, "cast into Tartarus", found only here. Darby describes the place; the KJV calls it hell.

records.change: "for ever" bracketed in the reserved darkness
records.note: "For ever" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; it may come from Jude 13. Darby keeps the words in brackets as doubtful.

records.change: Omits the heavenly witnesses: "the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost"
records.note: The words are in no Greek manuscript before the 14th century; they came into the Textus Receptus from late Latin copies in Erasmus's third edition. The Trinity is taught elsewhere, as in Matthew 28:19.

records.change: Omits "there are three that bear witness in earth"
records.note: The words are the second half of the same addition (the Johannine Comma) and are in no early Greek manuscript.

records.change: Omits "and that ye may believe on the name of the Son"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; belief on the Son is still named in the verse.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: "transgresseth" becomes "goes forward"; second "of Christ" dropped
records.note: The Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus have parabainōn (transgresses); Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus have proagōn (goes ahead). The second "of Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the early manuscripts.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus and some later manuscripts but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: "only Lord God, and our Lord" becomes "only Master and Lord"
records.note: The Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus have "God"; P72, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus lack it. Darby's reading makes Jesus Christ the only Master and Lord.

records.change: Omits "wise"; adds "through Jesus Christ our Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "only wise God" and lacks the phrase about Christ; P72, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus lack "wise" and add "through Jesus Christ our Lord" and "before all time".

records.change: Omits "the beginning and the ending"; "Lord" becomes "Lord God"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "the beginning and the ending" and "Lord"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and most manuscripts lack the phrase and read "Lord God". The phrase stands in 21:6 and 22:13.

records.change: Omits "Christ" twice after "Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Ephraemi.

records.change: Omits "I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last"
records.note: The words are in some late manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Ephraemi or the Byzantine majority. Christ calls himself "the first and the last" in 1:17.

records.change: "hell" becomes "hades"; omits "Amen"
records.note: The Greek is hadēs in both. "Amen" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Ephraemi.

records.change: Omits "four and twenty" and "him that liveth for ever and ever"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Ephraemi or the Byzantine majority; the elders still fall down and worship.

records.change: "Hell followed with him" becomes "hades followed"
records.note: The Greek is hadēs in both; Darby keeps the Greek word for the realm of the dead where the KJV has "hell". A translation choice.

records.change: "the God of the earth" becomes "the Lord of the earth"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "God"; nearly all Greek manuscripts have "Lord", as in Zechariah 4:14.

records.change: Omits "and art to come"
records.note: The words are in some late manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Ephraemi. Here God has begun to reign, so the title looks to the present.

records.change: Omits "Christ" after "testimony of Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus and some later manuscripts but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Ephraemi or most Byzantine copies.

records.change: Omits "before the throne of God"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus and a few late manuscripts but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Ephraemi or the Byzantine majority.

records.change: Omits "O Lord"; "and shalt be" becomes "the holy one"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "O Lord" and "shalt be"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Ephraemi and nearly all others have "the holy one" (hosios). Beza conjectured "shalt be" to match 1:4.

records.change: Omits "the Lord" and "honour"
records.note: Both are in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Ephraemi; the praise is still to "our God".

records.change: "from God" bracketed as the fire's source
records.note: "From God" is in Sinaiticus, the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Alexandrinus. Darby keeps the words in brackets as doubtful.

records.change: "stand before God" becomes "standing before the throne"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "God"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority have "the throne", the great white throne of verse 11.

records.change: "death and hell" becomes "death and hades"
records.note: The Greek is hadēs in both; Darby keeps the Greek word for the realm of the dead where the KJV has "hell". A translation choice.

records.change: "hell" becomes "hades"; adds "[even] the lake of fire"
records.note: The Greek is hadēs in both. "The lake of fire" at the end is in Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority but not in the Textus Receptus.

records.change: "God shall wipe away" becomes "he shall wipe away"
records.note: "God" is in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Alexandrinus; God is the subject from verse 3.

records.change: Omits "of them which are saved" and "and honour"
records.note: Both are in the Textus Receptus but not in the early or most Byzantine manuscripts. Only the saved enter the city, as 21:27 says.

records.change: "do his commandments" becomes "wash their robes"
records.note: The Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus read "do his commandments"; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read "wash their robes". Washing robes in the Lamb's blood is also in 7:14.

records.change: "book of life" becomes "tree of life"
records.note: Almost all Greek manuscripts read "tree"; "book" entered the Textus Receptus through Erasmus, whose Greek copy lacked these verses and was supplied from the Latin. The book of life is still named in 3:5, 20:15 and 21:27.

records.change: "our Lord" becomes "the Lord"; "you all" becomes "all the saints"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "our" and "you all"; the Byzantine majority has "all the saints", Sinaiticus "the saints". Darby keeps "Christ".
